Прогноз: 1X (Getafe не проигрывает)

Getafe ’s form has taken a nosedive since matchday one, but they may fancy their chances of a return to winning ways against a Málaga side yet to collect a La Liga victory this term.

Match News and Current Form

Getafe’s testing start to the season showed no signs of abating as Thursday night’s 1-0 defeat to Real Betis stretched their winless league run to five matches (D2, L3). Their five-point haul in La Liga is half the amount that they had accumulated at this stage last season, but with each of those points having been picked up on home soil (W1, D2), where José Bordalás’ men are unbeaten in six outings across all competitions (W4, D2), there is hope of a return to form here. A lack of goals remains an issue though, with only one team netting fewer times than Azulones, while last season only bottom-of-the-table Real Oviedo scored less goals than Getafe.

Opening their campaign with a six-game winless run (D3, L3) suggests Málaga are struggling to adapt to life back in the top flight. The most recent of those was a 3-1 home defeat to Villarreal on Thursday, and their fortunes have been even worse on the road, where after three winless outings already this term (D1, L2), Los Albicelestes are winless in 14 La Liga away games (D3, L11). It’s not all doom and gloom for Juan Francisco Funes’ side, who are two points better off than at the same stage of their 2017/18 relegation campaign, a season in which they were beaten to nil on the road on matchday seven.

Head-to-Head History

Getafe have won five of the last seven H2Hs (L2), with each of those wins coming by a 1-0 scoreline.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Seven of Getafe’s last eight league games produced under 2.5 goals.

Getafe’s games this season have produced a league-low three first-half goals.

Málaga have had a league-low ten shots on target this season.

Málaga have scored first in a pre-round joint-league low of one game this term (L1).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Enes Ünal has scored ten of his last 12 goals after half-time, although his last four for Getafe served as their first of the game. Málaga will be hoping Chupe can extend his record of just one defeat from the 20 matches he has scored in for the club (W15, D4), but his club-high 15 shots this term have yielded just one goal.

Getafe’s Mario Martín is suspended. Málaga hope to have Adam Aznou back, but Jens Cajuste is still out.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

These teams seem to do better after the break, so backing the second half to be the highest scoring seems like a sensible selection.

Author: Matt Jones
